decision: Exclude candidate A in its current broad formulation. Do not start GPU experiments or kernel porting.

findings: Dispatcher uses sparse paths for SM80/SM120 and SM90/SM100; SM89 reaches the dense fallback.
Block selection pools Q/K, scores the pooled representations and applies top-k; query/key provenance matters more than accumulator dtype.
Sparse map helpers and the attention call are separate in source; this permits designing a controlled selector intervention, but has not been validated on RTX4090.
Input validator requires equal Q/K/V shapes; not a drop-in rectangular-query AR KV-cache interface.
SM90 FP8 uses the native CuTe path, while other architectures enter a separate fallback with a different V-scale contract.
The documented method retains summaries for non-exact blocks; it is not plain block dropping. Last point checked against author technical documentation, not all kernel internals.

design_corrections: Full-precision selector is a reference selector, not a proven optimal oracle.
Hold Q, quantized KV, scales, grouping, candidate universe, block budget, forced blocks, RoPE, normalization and nonselected-block handling fixed for selector-only interventions.
Use dense BF16 and dense-quantized outputs as separate anchors if attributing total quality loss or sparsity/quantization interaction.
Y_quant_route minus Y_fullprecision_route is a conditional output change. Loss differences can be negative; do not assume independent nonnegative error contributions.
Accumulator FP32 does not recover precision lost when selector summaries originate from quantized K.
Compare against a simple retained high-precision block summary with its actual storage, build and read costs before proposing a complex selector.
A same-k diagnostic is not a same-time or same-memory deployment comparison.
Only source/read-only review completed; no new algorithm, GPU validation or novelty establishment claimed.
initial_decision: Do not start a GPU study yet. Broad novelty claim overlaps prior work; an executable sparse baseline on the current GPU is not established.

reasons: The broad novelty claim overlaps existing quantization/sparsity and compressed-key retrieval work.
The checked LightForcing revision has no validated sparse dispatch path for SM89; this does not imply sparse attention is impossible on RTX4090.
The three-arm comparison identifies a conditional selector intervention; BF16 selection is not a proven optimal oracle.
reopen_only_with: A concrete failure condition not explained or solved by the closest method, with an exact source or reproducible observation.
Evidence that the condition matters for output quality or end-to-end resource use, beyond changing model domain or nominal bit width.
A feasible comparison baseline with actual sparse execution verified; code provenance and adaptation cost disclosed.

future_candidate_recommendation_requires: Closest prior work and pinned public implementation reviewed before recommendation.
Separate verified facts, untested hypotheses, and implementation gaps.
Compare with the strongest applicable simple baseline, including memory and end-to-end cost.
State a falsifiable prediction, minimum discriminating experiment and stopping rule before execution.
